Bethel
BETH-ul
proper noun (place)
Hebrew Beth-El (H1008), "house of God," from bayit ("house") + El ("God"). A town north of Jerusalem in the hill country, originally called Luz, renamed by Jacob.

See also: Bethel

📖 Biblical Definition

Bethel ("house of God") was one of the most significant places in the patriarchal and later history of Israel — a town north of Jerusalem where the LORD met Jacob, and which became, tragically, a center of idolatrous worship in the divided kingdom. The site first appears when Abraham pitched his tent and built an altar between Bethel and Ai (Gen 12:8). But it is chiefly associated with Jacob: fleeing from Esau, he slept there and saw the ladder reaching to heaven with the angels of God ascending and descending, and the LORD standing above it confirming the covenant promise. Jacob awoke and said, "Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not... this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven" (Gen 28:16-17); he named the place Bethel, "house of God" (it had been called Luz). Years later, the LORD called Jacob back to Bethel to build an altar and renew his vows (Gen 35:1-15). Bethel thus stands as a place of true encounter with God, where heaven touched earth and the covenant was confirmed — the very ladder the Lord Jesus would later apply to Himself as the true gate of heaven, the Mediator on whom the angels ascend and descend (John 1:51). Yet Bethel's later history is a tragic inversion: when the kingdom divided, Jeroboam I set up one of his two golden calves at Bethel (1 Kings 12:28-29), making the "house of God" a house of idols and a center of false worship for the northern kingdom. Amos and Hosea prophesied against it; the LORD called it not Bethel ("house of God") but Beth-aven ("house of vanity/iniquity," Hos 4:15). The good king Josiah later defiled and destroyed the altar there (2 Kings 23:15). Bethel's two histories — the gate of heaven and the house of idols — warn that the most sacred places can be corrupted, and that the name "house of God" is no protection where true worship is abandoned.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The town ("house of God") where Jacob saw the ladder to heaven and named the place (Gen 28); a true place of covenant encounter, prefiguring Christ the gate of heaven (John 1:51); later corrupted into a center of golden-calf worship by Jeroboam I (1 Kings 12:28-29).

BETHEL, proper noun. Hebrew Beth-El (H1008), "house of God"; a town north of Jerusalem, formerly Luz.

Where Abraham built an altar (Gen 12:8) and chiefly where Jacob saw the ladder to heaven and named the place (Gen 28:10-22).

Jacob: "this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven" (Gen 28:17); the LORD called him back to renew his vows there (Gen 35).

The ladder prefigures Christ, the true gate of heaven on whom the angels ascend and descend (John 1:51).

Corrupted by Jeroboam I into a golden-calf center (1 Kings 12:28-29); called Beth-aven ("house of vanity") by Hosea; destroyed by Josiah (2 Kings 23:15).

📖 Key Scripture

Genesis 28:16-17 — "And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place; and I knew it not. And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place! this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."

John 1:51 — "And he saith unto him, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man."

1 Kings 12:28-29 — "Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold... And he set the one in Bethel, and the other put he in Dan."

Hosea 4:15 — "Though thou, Israel, play the harlot, yet let not Judah offend; and come not ye unto Gilgal, neither go ye up to Bethaven, nor swear, The LORD liveth."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Bethel is corrupted when its glorious patriarchal history is severed from its later idolatry, when the ladder vision is missed as a type of Christ, or when the lesson that "house of God" can become "house of vanity" is overlooked.

expand to see more

Ladder-typology missed. Jacob's vision at Bethel — the ladder set up on earth reaching to heaven, with the angels of God ascending and descending, and the LORD above it — is not merely a remarkable dream. The Lord Jesus applied it directly to Himself: "ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man" (John 1:51). Christ is the true ladder, the true Bethel, the one Mediator who joins heaven and earth, the gate of heaven through whom alone men come to God. To read the Bethel vision without seeing Christ is to miss the One the vision was given to reveal.

House-of-God-to-house-of-vanity warning. Bethel's tragedy is that the place named "house of God" (Beth-El) became, under Jeroboam, a house of idols, so that the prophet renamed it "Beth-aven" — house of vanity or iniquity (Hos 4:15; 5:8). The same site that had been the gate of heaven became a gate to false worship. The warning is permanent: a sacred name is no guarantee of sacred reality. Churches, denominations, and institutions that bear the name "house of God" can become houses of vanity when they abandon true worship for idols of their own making. Josiah's later destruction of Bethel's altar (2 Kings 23:15) shows that God will judge the corruption of His own house.
